analysis: The trial succeeded with host-evaluated macro validation HR@10 of 0.565: Movies_and_TV 0.620, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.610, Electronics 0.405, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.625. Electronics was the weakest category. Allocated GPU time was 373.65 seconds. No matched control score or training curves were supplied, so these results do not establish whether relative-position biases improved accuracy or explain category differences. Test performance is unavailable.
code_summary: Trains one independent masked-history transformer per category, using seed 42 and selecting one checkpoint by validation HR@10, with NDCG@10 as a tie-breaker. Each network uses 96-dimensional embeddings, absolute positions, two bidirectional pre-normalized transformer blocks, two attention heads, and dropout 0.25. The architectural change adds jointly learned, zero-initialized per-head signed relative-distance attention biases, clipped at ±32. Training masks the final item plus 15% of interior items and uses sampled softmax with 512 uniform negatives, normalized tied item embeddings, learned item biases and score scale, and AdamW. The generated predictor restores the same architecture, appends a mask token to the history, routes all four datasets, and scores candidates using exactly one checkpoint per category.
